We're not allowed to guess at who might arrive via the draft, or who a team might trade for or sign. We'll take the current roster and do the best we can based on aging curves, likely development (or slippage) and contract status.

The Atlanta Hawks are a team that has nearly everything but a clear first-option superstar. Onyeka Okongwu and Nickeil Alexander-Walker provide spacing and versatile defense at below-market prices, the books are very clean and rookie Kingston Flemings offers youthful upside.

Jalen Johnson still feels like more of a No. 2 on a dangerous team, but he's the man for now and has to be the pick in the absence of anyone with his level of proven production and growth potential. The best thing about the 24-year-old is the five-year, $150 million deal that'll keep him underpaid through 2029-30. With no one on the roster currently making more than that, there's room to add someone above him in the pecking order.
That said, Johnson made the All-NBA Third Team and averaged 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds and 7.9 assists last year.
So the second-best thing about him is that there's a non-zero chance he becomes a true superstar while still only making $30 million per season.

Though he'll be in his 30s by then, Jayson Tatum still pretty clearly projects to be the Boston Celtics' best player in three years. If it's not him, it'll be someone who's not currently on the roster.

That's no knock on guys like Hugo Gonzalez and Jordan Walsh, who should only be in their early primes by 2029, but those two are role players. Other options like Derrick White (32), Paul George (36) and Payton Pritchard (29) aren't at ages where you're expecting upward trajectories.
If Jaylen Brown were still on the team, maybe this would have been a more interesting exercise. Who's to say how Tatum might age in the wake of that 2025 Achilles tear?

Michael Porter Jr. probably has the distinction at the moment, and new addition Julius Randle is the one with multiple All-NBA nods on his resumé, but neither of those vets seem like big enough features in the Brooklyn Nets' long-term plans to be the team's best player in 2029.

Good. That allows us to consider the merits of far less-proven players, chiefly Brooklyn's last two top-10 picks: Egor Dëmin, who went eighth in 2025, and Mikel Brown Jr., the No. 6 pick in the most recent draft.

Brown is too much of a mystery to make him a responsible pick, while Dëmin shot 38.5 percent from deep last season and showed all the connective passing Brooklyn hoped for. A Summer League performance that saw Dëmin flash rapidly developing on-ball skills and scoring chops inside the arc puts him over the top.

The Nets have loads of young candidates who might only be a breakout away from changing this prediction. Ben Saraf, Nolan Traoré and Noah Clowney have all had their moments, and Clowney is the oldest of the group at just 22.
Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨
The Charlotte Hornets only have two realistic candidates, but Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller both have so much promise that this is the toughest toss-up we've encountered so far.

Knueppel is coming off the best shooting season we've ever seen from a rookie and is three years younger than Miller. What's more, the plus-2.8 Box Plus/Minus Knueppel produced last year as a rookie (while averaging 18.5 points on a 63.3 true shooting percentage) was significantly better than anything Miller managed in any of his first three seasons.

It's still tough to downplay Miller's upside as a potential two-way superstar wing. He has the rangy frame, high-wire athleticism and self-sufficient scoring craft teams covet, along with the physical profile of a three-level scorer who, with some development, might be able to guard the opponent's top wing threat.
Knueppel's floor is exceptionally high, but it's hard to argue he has a ceiling like Miller's.
We're going with the riskier option and choosing Miller. The takeaway here should be that Charlotte has two great cracks at a cornerstone.

Caleb Wilson is a bold choice here, considering he hasn't played a minute of NBA action yet. Josh Giddey is a much more established stat-stuffer, and Matas Buzelis is sitting right there with two seasons of experience at age 21. He's coming off a very strong second campaign marked by averages of 16.3 points and 5.8 boards along with intriguing development as a three-point threat.

Wilson, though, has the high-end draft pedigree as the No. 4 pick in a loaded lottery. It also helps that he used Summer League to flash completely unexpected jump-shooting prowess to go with his top-one-percent athleticism at the forward spot.

Buzelis is far from a slouch in the open floor, but Wilson might be a game-changer. We're speculating pretty hard here, but plenty of early signs are emerging that Wilson is going to have some real offensive skills to pair with a high-revving motor and elite finishing.
The Cleveland Cavaliers need Evan Mobley to be their best player right now , so he'd better be their top talent three seasons into the future.

Mobley disappointed last year relative to expectations. Ahead of 2025-26, most believed he'd build on a brilliant 2024-25 that saw him nearly triple his three-point attempt rate while posting a career-best 37.3 percent accuracy mark. Burying the lede, the 6'11" big man also won Defensive Player of the Year in 2024-25 and made his first All-NBA team.

Put together a season like that, and people are going to be a little bummed when you only follow it up with similar per-game averages on reduced efficiency. The thought was that Mobley was leaving Earth's orbit as a superstar. Instead, he leveled off.

Ahead of his age-25 season, Mobley is still among the top two-way frontcourt players in the sport. He's entering his prime, has already been officially recognized as one of the NBA's premier defenders and is a good bet to continue the offensive growth he's flashed in the past.
Barring a return to form from likely Hall-of-Famer Kyrie Irving, Cooper Flagg is going to be the Dallas Mavericks' best player in 2026-27.
Those who are particularly high on Flagg after a rookie season that included more offensive competency than anticipated might believe he'll be Dallas' top talent regardless of what Irving does.
Flagg's capability as a distributor and scorer were surprises, even if the extra workload produced a worse defensive performance than expected.

Assuming he continues his growth trajectory as a first-option on offense while coming closer to the All-Defense status many took as a given, Flagg should be one of the 10 best two-way players in the league within the time horizon we're considering.
Unless Dallas somehow adds a player with even greater potential, Flagg is one of the easiest choices of this entire exercise.

Nikola Jokić will play his age-34 season in 2029-30, putting him outside his prime but still making him highly likely to be an All-NBA force. Maybe if you're convinced that his relatively limited athleticism means he doesn't have a half-step to lose, Jokić could suffer a steep decline.
More likely, his unsurpassed processing speed, passing eye and scoring touch will allow him to remain the top offensive option in the league deep into his 30s.

The only potential hiccup here is trusting Jokić will be a member of the Denver Nuggets three years from now. There were financial reasons for him to turn down extensions both last offseason and this past summer; he can get larger annual salaries and longer deals by waiting. There are certainly no signals the three-time MVP wants to play anywhere else.

That said, Denver has cut salary via trades and had trouble surrounding Jokić with the level of talent he deserves for several seasons since the 2022-23 title. It wouldn't be a shock if he determined the Nuggets don't give him the best chance to win another championship.
As it stands, Jokić can hit unrestricted free agency in the summer of 2027.
The question isn't whether Cade Cunningham will be the Detroit Pistons' top player three years from now. It's how big the gap will be between him and his team's second option.
Cunningham is only just now entering his prime after proving himself as a legitimate MVP candidate and postseason-minted superstar in 2025-26. He'll hold that level or improve on it through 2029.

Detroit is currently squeezing Jalen Duren in restricted free agency because he, unlike Cunningham, failed to maintain his value in the playoffs. Ausar Thompson is eligible for an extension, but his shooting and playmaking limitations are major hindrances to the Pistons' roster-building effort. If he can't get substantially better on offense, he'll take himself out of the running for Detroit's No. 2 spot behind Cunningham and might even wind up out of the team's plans entirely.
We're only copping out like this once because the Golden State Warriors are on a timeline that screams they'll be a completely different organization before three years have elapsed.

Odds are, Stephen Curry, Draymond Green and Steve Kerr will have retired by the start of the 2029-30 season. The franchise will have either pivoted to a full rebuild or, more likely, lured an in-prime star in free agency. Maybe they'll have done both by then. Life cycles around the league are only accelerating, so anything's possible.
The only certainty here is that nobody on the current roster appears to be a cornerstone capable of holding up through three more seasons. Whoever takes the mantle from Steph isn't on the team yet.

Alperen Sengün is only five months older than Amen Thompson and already has a 2-0 lead in career All-Star games. You'd have to possess a very strong belief in Thompson's ability to grow as a shooter to choose him over his more accomplished teammate.

Defensively, Thompson is at a level Sengün is unlikely to reach. But for Thompson to become Houston's best player, he will need to improve substantially on the 21.9 percent he shot from three-point range. Elite wings generally need at least a credible perimeter shot, and his shooting currently presents a major obstacle to that outcome.

Reed Sheppard should get a smidgen of consideration here, but he needs to prove he's a full-time starter before we project him as the Houston Rockets' alpha by 2029. Last year's 13.5 points per game, 39.4 percent shooting from deep and sixth-place finish in Sixth Man of the Year voting were a good start, but the No. 3 pick from the 2024 draft has a ways to go.
Pascal Siakam is probably a year too old to make him a safe fallback choice for those too concerned about Tyrese Haliburton's health to make him the selection for the Indiana Pacers.
Three years from now, Siakam will be entering his age-35 season. He's held up well so far and was an All-Star in each of the last two years, but the aging curve comes for everyone eventually.

Haliburton is only 26, six years younger than Siakam. Considering the heights he reached before tearing his Achilles, it feels safe to assume he'll still be in his prime (and that his prime will resemble the last few seasons) by 2029.

Lest we forget, Haliburton led Indy to within a win of a championship, already has an assist crown to go with his two All-NBA nods and is on the very shortest list of the league's most singularly transformative offensive forces.
He'll still be a superstar three years from now.
We're getting bold here by going with LA Clippers' recent lottery pick Keaton Wagler over two-time All-Star Darius Garland.

After coming aboard in the James Harden trade last year, Garland looked like the same guy who played a major role on some excellent Cavs teams. In 19 games with the Clips, he put up 19.9 points and 6.4 assists on a 47.1/43.8/86.0 shooting split. Entering his age-27 season, he could make this prediction look bad by simply holding onto that level of production.

Garland is set to earn $44.9 million in 2027-28 before his contract expires. Do the Clippers intend to extend him for what seems certain to be at least $50 million per year when they just drafted someone who plays his same position?
Wagler will only be 22 and still on his rookie-scale deal in three seasons. He could either surpass Garland in effectiveness or simply be the better value by then.

Luka Dončić's current contract is set to expire after 2028-29 if he plays it out all the way through his player option that season. Technically, he's not guaranteed to be on the Los Angeles Lakers in three years.
Dončić didn't choose to join the Lakers and has never really had control over his destination. It's possible he'll want to test free agency.

More likely: Dončić will decline his player option and sign a five-year deal worth over $400 million in the summer of 2028. Assuming that outcome, he'll be one of the half-dozen best players in the league as he enters the later stages of his prime—more than qualifying him for "best player on the team" status.

The bar Dončić set early in his career by making five straight All-NBA First Teams from his age-20 to age-24 seasons will be difficult to clear, but he could regress from that level and still be Los Angeles' obvious top threat.

If he makes good on the statistical profile that suggested he should have been the top draftee in his class, Cam Boozer might be the Memphis Grizzlies' best player when he debuts in October. Three years from now, the gap between him and Memphis' No. 2 option may only be wider.

Boozer has limitations. He doesn't have the run-and-jump burst many teams prioritize in their forwards. In college and during a brief Summer League showing, he did what his believers expected by compensating for those shortcomings with uncommon feel, passing acumen, ball-handling and shooting potential.
What Boozer lacks in speed and bounce, he can make up for with cleverness, power and skill.
To justify the price they paid, the Miami Heat had better hope Giannis Antetokounmpo is still their best player in three years.

If he's not—either because he left after choosing not to extend his contract or because his skills and health declined substantially—the Heat will be in a brutal spot. Though Antetokounmpo's desire to land in Miami may have slightly diminished the trade package headed back to the Milwaukee Bucks, his onboarding came at the cost of an entire lineup's worth of useful players and four first-round assets.

If this roster build doesn't work, the Heat don't have many good outs. Though they could trade Bam Adebayo or Giannis (at reduced value in the hypothetical where he's no longer a superstar), a move like that might not even put them back to neutral from a rebuilding perspective.

The recent set of 2026 draftees, AJ Green and Gary Trent Jr. (for now), are the only players ticketed to collect salaries from the Bucks in 2029-30. That makes No. 10 pick Brayden Burries the easy choice.

Burries' eye-opening Summer League work is doing all the lifting here, but it's hard not to be encouraged by a guy who came into the draft cycle billed as a good defender who could shoot, only to watch him show unexpected on-ball utility. As the Bucks start over, he's the highest-upside piece they have.

Ryan Rollins is a better guard right now and is only heading into his age-25 season. Because his current deal is too team-friendly to make an extension realistic, he's almost assured of hitting unrestricted free agency after the upcoming season. Betting on him to stay in Milwaukee is a risk.

In good news for the Bucks, they also have Kasparas Jakucionis and Kel'el Ware in the up-and-coming category. The former will be a restricted free agent after 2028-29 and could develop into a high-end starter by then.
Here's hoping this pick eases the minds of Minnesota Timberwolves fans who don't love the barely audible whispers that Anthony Edwards is the latest big star other teams are starting to circle.

The Wolves aren't quite all-in on this core after trading assets for LaMelo Ball, but they're running out of ways to change course if this build doesn't work. We've seen this movie before, and it often ends with the incumbent star moving on after several years of banging into a sub-Finals ceiling.

Edwards is fresh off his fourth straight All-Star campaign and has improved his scoring average and true shooting percentage in every season of his career. He could level off right where he's at and pile up top-10 MVP finishes through our three-year time cutoff.
That said, only entering his age-25 season, Edwards should be expected to keep improving.
Nobody Minnesota adds will be a better player than Edwards. Whether or not he's still on the team is the only question.
Choosing Derik Queen here is a bet that the knack he showed for creative and relatively efficient scoring in college will return as he gets further into his pro career. It'll have to.

Queen is undersized at 6'9" for the center spot and doesn't seem likely to excel as a back-line option. That means his craft, passing and foul-drawing will need to improve as he works to turn himself into a power forward through whom the offense runs.
Last year's 79.5 free-throw percentage is a hopeful sign Queen might someday feature a three-point shot worth honoring, and he'll have to be a threat from deep to make any of this work.
Jeremiah Fears has the athletic burst to warrant consideration, and if Trey Murphy III is still on the team in three years, he's easily the safest choice.

The New York Knicks are a veteran team with no projectable youth, unless you think Mohamed Diawara is in for a leap or two. The unlikelihood of a 20-something reaching stardom makes Jalen Brunson the clear choice from among the championship-winning core.

An All-NBA honoree three years running and coming off a no-brainer Finals MVP, Brunson will play his age-30 season in 2026-27. Given his craft and shooting ability, he should age well for a small guard. Decline can come early for that player type, but Brunson isn't dependent on a lightning-quick first step or the ability to rise over larger defenders at the rim. His pivot game, deft touch and herky-jerky style will still be flummoxing defenders as he heads into post-prime territory.
Natural wear and tear will probably mean Brunson is no longer in the MVP conversation by 2029, but he should still be a clear All-Star.
Oklahoma City Thunder: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

The gap between Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder's other options—principally Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren—is wide enough today to price in growth for the youngsters and still go with the two-time MVP.

Williams is a tremendous two-way force when healthy, but he's not all that far removed from real questions about his fitness as a first option during OKC's non-SGA minutes. It feels safe to assume that Gilgeous-Alexander, who'll be starting his age-31 season in 2029, will remain an MVP candidate and still be arguably the best offensive weapon in the league.
Holmgren is like Williams in that he's going to make several more All-NBA appearances but almost certainly never reach the MVP tier of difference-makers that SGA has belonged to since 2022-23.
The only real question here is how many more of those trophies Gilgeous-Alexander will collect over the next three seasons. Let's put the over-under at 1.5.
The pendulum has swung pretty far toward the negative on Paolo Banchero, whose production slipped last year in a second-straight non-award-worthy season.
After winning Rookie of the Year and making the All-Star team in his sophomore follow-up, Banchero has battled declining efficiency and faced questions about his fitness as an alpha offensive weapon.
All this just as his supermax extension kicks in.
Maybe Banchero's star has dimmed, but he's only 23 and is still quite clearly the Orlando Magic's highest-ceiling player.

He's a foul-drawing machine whose combination of strength and skill should only make him harder to guard without hacking as he gains experience. And at 31.7 percent from deep for his career, he's not a hopeless case from long range.

Assuming these last two relatively tough seasons encourage Banchero to move the ball more freely and cut the junk food from his shot diet, he should be the Magic's top talent in 2029, when he'll be entering his age-27 season.

VJ Edgecombe's standout rookie season and clear fitness for playoff competition give some pause here, but we can't overthink things in the wake of Tyrese Maxey piling up 28.3 points per game and making an All-NBA team last season.

Skeptics might note that Maxey, 25, might be a candidate for early slippage when his blinding speed starts to go. Given his heavy minute totals (he led the league at 38.0 per game last year), the loss of his peak athleticism is a concern. Fortunately for Maxey, he's a high-volume three-point shooter who sits at 37.7 percent for his career and has been much better than that when not tasked with taking so many tough ones.
Perhaps just as importantly, Maxey has tremendous touch on his floater and doesn't need to get all the way to the basket to remain a serious paint-scoring threat.
Edgecombe could make an All-Star game by 2029, and maybe Jaylen Brown will still be hanging on as a star by then. But Maxey is pretty clearly the pick for Philly.

In an ideal world, the 2029 version of Khaman Maluach would be a dominant defensive center who also spreads the floor as a long-range shooter. When players with his immense size and work ethic pick up the game at 14, it feels slightly less irresponsible to make such wild projections.
Maluach is a very long way from meeting those optimistic forecasts. Devin Booker, meanwhile, is an established star who seems interested in finishing his career with the Phoenix Suns.

Booker will almost assuredly be overpaid on a $69 million salary for 2029-30, his age-33 season. But he's such a polished and professional scorer that he should retain plenty of effectiveness between now and then.

One other factor in Booker's favor: Phoenix is among the teams most bereft of future picks that might bring in a young, high-upside star. It's hard to imagine the Suns adding someone through the draft who'll overtake Booker as he declines.

Deni Avdija came into the league and established himself primarily as a defensive forward who could chip in just enough offense as long as you didn't ask him to shoot too much. Flash forward and he's now one of the best downhill attackers and offensive self-starters in the league.
If you think a guy who could transform himself like that is done growing at 26, you've got another thing coming.

Though new Portland Trail Blazers owner Tom Dundon is pinching pennies all over the place, he seems willing to spend on the roster. He'll have to if he wants to keep Avdija around when his dirt-cheap contract expires after 2027-28, when he'll earn a laughably low $11.9 million.

Scoot Henderson could still pop, and Donovan Clingan will become more interesting if he continues his development as a spacer. But if Avdija comes back on a new deal, he'll still be the man in Portland.
Say it with me, Sacramento Kings, so that we may speak it into existence and avert another several seasons of irrelevance: Darius Acuff Jr. will not be a bust.
Feel free to repeat that as many times as it takes to manifest an outcome Sacramento hopes for but is far from guaranteed to see.

Acuff has work to do if he's going to make a positive impact on winning. The rookie's small frame and inefficient showing in Summer League did not quiet concerns about his future. But if not him, who even profiles as a realistic option on the Kings roster?
Keegan Murray, who's somehow declining in his mid-20s? Domantas Sabonis, who's already on the wrong side of 30? Nique Clifford?
So let's spend a few paragraphs making the case for Harrison Barnes. See, the thing you're really not considering about locker-room sages is...

OK, we all know there's no point in choosing anyone but Victor Wembanyama. That was just an attempt to make this mildly interesting. A better and much more realistic head-fake would have involved talking up Dylan Harper as an alternative based on Wemby's occasionally concerning health issues and Harper's pretty clear future as an All-NBA force.
Even that would be too disingenuous to maintain for more than a sentence or two.

Wemby is the reigning Defensive Player of the year and should win that award every season for the next decade or so while adding layers upon layers to his offensive game. If he doesn't have an MVP or two by 2029, it'll be a surprise.

Scottie Barnes would have to endure a bizarre slide as he enters what should be his prime, and one of the Toronto Raptors' intriguing youngsters would need to develop far beyond role-player status to make this pick interesting.

Considering Barnes is coming off his most complete regular season and a stunningly good playoff performance (24.1 points, 8.6 assists, 6.1 rebounds), he doesn't seem like a candidate for slippage. And while Collin Murray-Boyles and rookie Allen Graves are going to figure prominently in Toronto's success going forward, those two don't come with obvious star upside.

Barnes has already made a couple of All-Star games, finished fifth in DPOY voting last year and may now be moving into a phase where he can be his team's offensive engine in a postseason setting. At 25, he's also not done improving.
The Utah Jazz have two immensely promising younger options in rookie Darryn Peterson and second-year wing Ace Bailey. Either could become stars in three years.
Complicating matters, they also have two much more established in-prime options in Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

It's tempting to go with JJJ here. He's got three All-Defensive nods, a DPOY award and multiple seasons shooting at least 37.0 percent from long range. He's making an average of $51 million through 2029-30 for a reason.
We still haven't discussed Keyonte George, though, and he falls somewhere between Utah's speculative prospects and the more established Jackson.

In his age-22 season, George exploded. He put up 23.6 points per game, hit 37.1 percent from deep on good volume and compromised defenders often enough to shoot 7.1 free throws per game, making 89.2 percent of them. He might be a bigger, more aggressive, craftier Darius Garland, which is basically a perennial All-NBA candidate if he can stay healthy.
The risk with George is that his breakout came in 54 mostly meaningless games last year. It's impossible to be sure what he did was real, but we're going with him anyway.
Unless it's an unusually weak class (hey there, 2024!), the team that selects first should be deeply disappointed if the guy they pick doesn't wind up atop their depth chart in three years' time.
The Washington Wizards don't have to worry about that. AJ Dybantsa is going to be a star.

Maybe he'll have some flaws if his long-range shot doesn't develop as hoped, but huge, athletic wings who know how to win one-on-one matchups and have every defensive tool a team could want don't tend to flop.

Dybantsa has obstacles in vets like Trae Young and Anthony Davis, and the former is locked into a deal that'll keep him on the team through 2029 barring a trade. The Wizards are also stocked with other prospects like Alex Sarr, Kyshawn George and Tre Johnson who could all theoretically ascend.
In the end, Dybantsa is a No. 1 pick in a strong draft class who is supposed to take over this team sooner than later. He will.
Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .
Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: El nuevo desafío asiático de Luis Guil: "Si en el Real Madrid no consigues resultados, sabes lo que puede pasar"
articles.standfirst: Luis Guil es el nuevo seleccionador de Jordania
articles.summary: Luis Guil es el nuevo seleccionador de Jordania
articles.body: Luis Guil tiene nuevo destino. Meses después de su salida del Real Madrid, el ex ayudante de Sergio Scariolo en el conjunto blanco y en la selección, dirigirá a la selección de Jordania. Será su segunda aventura asiática tras Japón y tendrá el reto de clasificar al equipo jordano para el Mundial 2027 y crear una estructura de baloncesto en la Federación. Desde Taiwán, en plena preparación de la Ventana de Agosto, atendió la llamada de Radio MARCA. Un proyecto que va mucho más allá de las próximas ventanas de agosto: “No solamente es clasificar al equipo para el Mundial, sino crear una forma, una identidad de juego dentro de la Federación de Jordania”. El objetivo inmediato es ambicioso: Jordania marcha segunda de su grupo, con cinco victorias y una derrota, en una fase en la que se mide a Australia, Nueva Zelanda y Filipinas. Guil reconoce que la propuesta le sedujo especialmente por la posibilidad de trabajar también con las categorías inferiores y construir una estructura común para todo el baloncesto jordano. “La federación me proponía liderar todo el tema de las categorías inferiores junto con la senior, e ir en un mismo camino, un poco parecido a lo que se hizo en la Federación, en la selección española, en los últimos años”, explica. El técnico, con amplia experiencia en las categorías de formación españolas y tras su paso por Japón, considera que Jordania tiene una buena base para crecer y competir de nuevo en un Mundial. Su primer contacto con el nuevo equipo ha sido, además, de máxima exigencia. “Todo ha sido muy rápido”, admite Guil, que pasó apenas 24 horas en Ammán antes de viajar a Taiwán para disputar un torneo internacional. Para preparar las ventanas, el entrenador apuesta por conocer primero a fondo a sus jugadores y adaptar sus ideas a las características de la plantilla. Entre los nombres destacados está Rondae Hollis-Jefferson, además de jugadores con experiencia internacional y universitarios estadounidenses. Guil también se apoyará en su conocimiento de Australia y Filipinas y en los contactos que conserva de su etapa en Asia. La nueva aventura llega después de una temporada en el Real Madrid que terminó sin títulos y con la salida de Scariolo y su cuerpo técnico. Guil no esconde que le habría gustado otro desenlace, pero entiende la decisión: “Pena te da que no consigas los resultados, pero sabes a qué club vas, vas al Real Madrid, con el objetivo de ganarlo todo, absolutamente todo”. Pese a ello, hace un balance muy positivo de su etapa en el conjunto blanco: “Me siento halagado por ser elegido por el Madrid y por Sergio” y destaca especialmente haber disputado una Euroliga de máximo nivel y una Final Four que el equipo tuvo al alcance hasta el último tiro. Y si hay una figura determinante en su carrera, esa es Sergio Scariolo. Guil, que trabajó durante años a su lado en la selección española y volvió a hacerlo en Madrid, lo define como “un referente total” tanto por sus conocimientos técnico-tácticos como por su método de trabajo. “Es una persona que crea formas de trabajo, deja un legado en la forma de trabajar”, asegura. Ahora, ya como primer entrenador de una selección, afronta el desafío de aplicar todo ese aprendizaje a Jordania: intentar alcanzar el Mundial de Qatar 2027 y, al mismo tiempo, construir los cimientos de un proyecto que vaya mucho más allá de una sola competición.

El técnico, con amplia experiencia en las categorías de formación españolas y tras su paso por Japón, considera que Jordania tiene una buena base para crecer y competir de nuevo en un Mundial. Su primer contacto con el nuevo equipo ha sido, además, de máxima exigencia. “Todo ha sido muy rápido”, admite Guil, que pasó apenas 24 horas en Ammán antes de viajar a Taiwán para disputar un torneo internacional. Para preparar las ventanas, el entrenador apuesta por conocer primero a fondo a sus jugadores y adaptar sus ideas a las características de la plantilla. Entre los nombres destacados está Rondae Hollis-Jefferson, además de jugadores con experiencia internacional y universitarios estadounidenses. Guil también se apoyará en su conocimiento de Australia y Filipinas y en los contactos que conserva de su etapa en Asia. La nueva aventura llega después de una temporada en el Real Madrid que terminó sin títulos y con la salida de Scariolo y su cuerpo técnico. Guil no esconde que le habría gustado otro desenlace, pero entiende la decisión: “Pena te da que no consigas los resultados, pero sabes a qué club vas, vas al Real Madrid, con el objetivo de ganarlo todo, absolutamente todo”. Pese a ello, hace un balance muy positivo de su etapa en el conjunto blanco: “Me siento halagado por ser elegido por el Madrid y por Sergio” y destaca especialmente haber disputado una Euroliga de máximo nivel y una Final Four que el equipo tuvo al alcance hasta el último tiro. Y si hay una figura determinante en su carrera, esa es Sergio Scariolo. Guil, que trabajó durante años a su lado en la selección española y volvió a hacerlo en Madrid, lo define como “un referente total” tanto por sus conocimientos técnico-tácticos como por su método de trabajo. “Es una persona que crea formas de trabajo, deja un legado en la forma de trabajar”, asegura. Ahora, ya como primer entrenador de una selección, afronta el desafío de aplicar todo ese aprendizaje a Jordania: intentar alcanzar el Mundial de Qatar 2027 y, al mismo tiempo, construir los cimientos de un proyecto que vaya mucho más allá de una sola competición.

articles.title: James Harden Joins LeBron James, Steph Curry, KD in Elite NBA Earnings Club After $97M Cavs Contract
articles.summary: James Harden is on track to become the fourth player in NBA history to make more than half a billion dollars in career earnings.
articles.body:
James Harden is on track to become the fourth player in NBA history to make more than half a billion dollars in career earnings.

Harden has agreed to a three-year, $97 million contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

That brings Harden's career earnings to a total of $511 million, per Charania .

Here's a look at where Harden ranks among the highest-earning players in NBA history, courtesy of Spotrac .

Harden's new contract with the Cavs includes a player option and a trade kicker, Charania reported.

The news comes shortly after the Cavaliers completed a five-team sign-and-trade deal to bring in Peyton Watson.

The Cavs had about $22.9 million in first apron space before signing Harden, per Spotrac .

How his contract is constructed could impact whether the team exceeds the first apron this season. His $32 million average annual salary means the Cavs will remain below the second apron.

Harden spent most of the last three seasons with the Los Angeles Clippers, most recently re-signing with the club last offseason on a two-year, $81.5 million deal with a player option.

He was traded to the Cavaliers in February before declining that $42.3 million player option in June.

Harden will turn 37 later this month. He's on track to join James as the second player in NBA history to sign a deal with more than $90 million in guaranteed money at that age or older, according to Charania .

His agent discussed both two- and three-year contracts with the Cavaliers before finalizing the three-year deal, Charania reported.

Harden ranked No. 46 among the world's highest-paid athletes last year by Forbes .

According to Forbes, Harden earned $39.6 million in salary last season while receiving $16 million in off-court earnings in part thanks to partnerships with brands like Adidas.

Harden averaged 20.5 points, 7.7 assists and 4.8 rebounds in 26 regular-season games with the Cavs before averaging 19.2 points through 18 playoff contests during the team's run to the Eastern Conference Finals.

The Cavaliers will now hope their investment in retaining Harden will help this team go on an even deeper playoff run in 2027.

articles.title: James Harden será el cuarto jugador mejor pagado de la historia
articles.standfirst: 'La Barba' seguirá en Cleveland tres temporadas más, la tercera como opción del jugador
articles.summary: 'La Barba' seguirá en Cleveland tres temporadas más, la tercera como opción del jugador
articles.body: Era uno de los agentes libres más atractivos del mercado aunque nadie esperaba que cambiara de aires. Y no lo hará. James Harden, tras renunciar a su opción de jugador en junio y 42 millones, llegó a un acuerdo con los Cavs para seguir en el equipo las tres próximas temporadas con un contrarto por 97 millones de dólares. La tercera temporada será una opción de jugador. El acuerdo convertirá a 'La Barba' en el cuarto jugador que más dinero haya ganado en la historia de la NBA. De hecho será el cuarto que supere el límite de los 500 millones ganados a lo largo de una carrera (511 para 'La Barba') después de LeBron James, Kevin Durant y Stephen Curry. En pocos días, 26 de agosto, Harden cumplirá los 37 años y podría estender su carrera hasta los 40 si cumple todo el contrato con Cleveland. Es el segundo jugador de la historia que firma un contrato garantizado por más de 90 millones a los 37 años. El otro, claro, fue LeBron. Además, 'La Barba' que inicia su temporada 18 en la NBA, podrá redondear su trayectoria con las 20 temporadas en activo. Harden, en lugar de preferir los 42 millones de su último año, prefirió trabajar con los Cavs en dos escenarios, un contrato de dos años y otro de tres, el último como opción de jugador, que es el que ha prevalecido. Además el tiempo de espera ha permitido a los Cavs trabajar en el resto de su plantilla. La opción elegida permite a los Cavs pagar a Harden en tres años en lugar de dos y así poder transitar por debajo del primer y segundos aprons en el límite salarial. Si 'La Barba' cumple con su trasuectoria, los Cavs no acabarán con récord negativo de victorias en la Liga regular, nunca lo ha hecho Harden en todos los equipos que ha jugado. Pero eso es un pronóstico fácil de hacer un equipo que aspira a todo en el Este.

articles.title: Jokic gana a Wembanyama rozando el triple-doble
articles.standfirst: El serbio se despachó con 20 puntos, nueve rebotes y ocho asistencias ante Francia
articles.summary: El serbio se despachó con 20 puntos, nueve rebotes y ocho asistencias ante Francia
articles.body: Serbia y Francia eligieron jugar un par de amistosos antes de afrontar los dos compromisos de las Ventanas de clasificación para el Mundial de 2027. Y el caso es que eligieron hacerlo uno contra otro, convirtiendo su doble enfrentamiento en la fiesta del baloncesto antes de los partidos oficiales de la FIBA. No está nada mal pasar varias semanas sin competición y retomar la actividad con un duelo entre dos de las mejores selecciones del mundo y dos de los mejores jugadores del planeta. Serbia se llevó el primer duelo, el jugado en Belgrado, este jueves 90-87. Lo ganó en un choque que llegó muy igualado al descanso pero en el que los locales fueron mejores tras la reanudación. Pero lo que el mundo del baloncesto quería ver es a Nikola Jokic y Victor Wembanyama bailando en la pintura, uno contra otro en un duelo en el que ya se puede fantasear de cara al próximo Mundial... si los dos equipos se clasifican. El 'Joker' fue mejor. Las dudas de si iban a jugar mucho o poco incluso de si iban a coincidir se disiparon cuando ambos se midieron en el salto incial del partido. Luego varias acciones como un taponazo del francés cuando el serbio trataba de machacar, un par de mates de 'Wemby', uno de espaldas de los que tanto abusa con los Spurs, o varias lecciones al poste del serbio que puso en juego más arsenal ofensivo que su rival. A estos partidos los llaman amistosos (friendly match), pero de amistosos tienen poco. Sirven para rodar a los equipos , recién acoplados, pero en un partido entre Jokic y Wembanyama, todos los focos apuntan a los dos jugadores interiores más dominantes del mundo. Serbia tuvo que ganar el partido dos veces. Llegó al descanso con una ventaja mínima, 46-45, tras una ligera ventaja francesa, 29-34, mediado el segundo cuarto. En la reanudación el equipo local pareció entrar con mejor pie y empezó a construir una ventaja que pareció definitiva cuando quedaban 5:41 para el final del partido, 82-69. Eran los mejores momentos de Jokic que dominaba el choque con números que se acercaron al triple-doble (para él no hay amistosos, un partido es un partido y acabó con 20 puntos, 9 rebotes y 8 asistencias  y 33 de valoración). También eran momentos de inspiración para Milutinov (15), Avramovic (13) y Dobric (12). Pero Francia no había dicho su última palabra. Un parcial de 0-9 en dos minutos colocó el 86-83 a falta de 1:01 que se apretó mucho más a falta de 11 segundos con el 88-86. Dos tiros libres de Avramovic y otros dos de Dobric colocaron el definitivo 90-87 que cerró el primer gran duelo entre dos colosos. Wembanyama perdió el duelo colectivo y el individual, ofreciendo algunos chispazos pero con una segunda mitad muy floja. Firmó 10 puntos, 5 rebotes  y 2 asistencias para 10 de valoración. El mejor anotador en Francia fue Noua (14), seguido por Francisco (13) y por Gerald Ayayi (10). En materia reboteadora, el propio Ayayi y Noua igualaron los cinco rebotes de 'Wemby'. Ambos equipos continuarán su preparación este domingo (18.00) en la devolución de visita de Serbia, esta vez en suelo francés (en el CO’Met Arena de Orleans). Una nueva ocasión de poder disfrutar de dos de los mejores jugadores de su tiempo.

articles.title: Un test mundial para España
articles.standfirst: La selección juega el torneo internacional de Tenerife ante Nigeria y Bélgica
articles.summary: La selección juega el torneo internacional de Tenerife ante Nigeria y Bélgica
articles.body: En una exigente preparación para el Mundial, la selección femenina de baloncesto debe medirse a cinco equipos que estarán en la cita de Berlín. Ya lo hizo ante Alemania (60-65) en el primer test, un rival al que se volverá a enfrentar ya en el estreno del Mundial (4 de septiembre). Ahora llega el gran torneo internacional de Tenerife, con partidos ante Nigeria y Bélgica, y la gira se cerrará en Zaragoza, ante Mali, otro rival del grupo de España y China, antes de viajar a Alemania. El equipo que dirige Miguel Méndez afronta un excelente torneo en Tenerife que da mucho brillo a la gira ‘Volvemos a soñar’. El Santiago Martín acoge tres grandes partidos empezando este mismo viernes, a las 21.00 horas (tdp), con un España - Nigeria, siguiendo el sábado con el Bélgica - Nigeria y cerrando el torneo el domingo con el España - Bélgica. En liza, las campeonas de África (Nigeria) y Europa (Bélgica) y equipos que, como España, buscarán estar en la lucha por las medallas en Berlín. El partido será muy espceial para dos jugadoras canarias, Elena Buenavida, nacida en Santa Cruz de Tenerife, y Maite Cazorla, en Las Palmas. Las dos jugarán ante su afición en un torneo que la escolta del Valencia Basket analizaba así: “Qué mejor que jugar contra dos rivales como Nigeria y Bélgica que son de lo más top del mundo”. Para ambas será un orgullo este test Mundial para España. Para el partido de este viernes ante Nigeria, al margen de las bajas por tener jugadoras en la WNBA, Méndez tendrá que hacer dos descartes en cada partido en su lista de 14 convocadas. En Nigeria, también sin alguna jugadora todavía en competición en la NBA, las referencias en el partido serán Ezinne Kalu, la líder y directora de juego, Murjanatu Musa, una jugadora muy dominnate en la pintura, y Victoria Macaulau, autora de 13,6 puntos de media en los partidos de clasificación para el Mundial.

articles.title: Nikola Jokic Says Wemby Could Be 'Best Ever,' Praises Spurs Star Ahead of FIBA World Cup Qualifiers
articles.summary: Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokić had high praise for San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama after they faced off in a friendly international matchup on Thursday.
articles.body:
Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokić had high praise for San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama after they faced off in a friendly international matchup on Thursday.

"He's definitely a special opponent just because how unique he is as a player, as a person," Jokić told reporters. "I don't see it as a rivalry. Do I take it a little bit more? No, I think I play every game the same way. But Victor definitely has the opportunity to be the most unique basketball player that we've ever seen. It only depends only on him, how well he's gonna fit, how well he's gonna work hard, how well he's gonna get to his spots, how well he's gonna treat his body. He definitely has the opportunity to be the best ever."

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

Jokić and Serbia ended up taking down Wembanyama and France by the final score of 90-87 in a friendly competition as both squads prepare for the start of FIBA World Cup European qualifiers.

Jokić finished with 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists while shooting 5-of-13 from the field. The three-time NBA MVP also hit nine of his 12 free throws.

Wembanyama recorded 10 points, five rebounds and two assists. He shot 3-of-9 from the field and 1-of-6 from behind the arc.

The 22-year-old has already established himself as one of the top players in the NBA, as he's coming off a 2025-26 campaign with San Antonio in which he earned unanimous Defensive Player of the Year honors and received an All-NBA First Team selection.

Wembanyama averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 3.1 blocks per game on 51.2/34.9/82.7 shooting splits. He helped the Spurs compile a 62-20 record before advancing to the NBA Finals.

While San Antonio ultimately fell short of a championship, the organization's future is still bright with Wembanyama leading the way.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers Appears to Tell Caitlin Clark to 'Calm Down' in Trending Video of Heated Exchange
articles.summary: Things got heated between Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers during the Dallas Wings' win over the Indiana Fever on Thursday.
articles.body:
Things got heated between Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers during the Dallas Wings' win over the Indiana Fever on Thursday.

While Clark argued with an official about a call, Bueckers appeared to tell the Fever star to "calm down."

Clark perhaps let her frustration boil over during what was a rough showing from her. She finished with just 10 points on 10-of-15 from the field and 2-of-8 from deep, adding nine assists and four boards.

Bueckers also wasn't at her best as she had 13 points, eight assists and six rebounds on 5-of-16 from the field and 0-of-2 from deep, but the Wings managed to leave with a win thanks to 32 points from Arike Ogunbowale.

While Clark and Bueckers are both still young, they've each turned into two of the best guards in the league.

Clark is putting up 22.1 points and 8.3 assists per game this year, making a serious case to win her first MVP. Bueckers, who is in just her second season, is averaging 20.5 points, 5.8 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game.

Clark's Fever are sitting in third place in the WNBA standings at 24-13, tied with the Las Vegas Aces. Buckers' Wings are in eighth place at 21-16 but are in good playoff position, sitting five games ahead of the ninth-placed Portland Fire.

Thursday was the last matchup between Clark and Bueckers this season, but the two very well could meet again in the postseason.

articles.title: Jokic: "Wembanyama tiene la oportunidad de ser único, de ser el mejor de la historia"
articles.standfirst: "Wembanyama es un rival especial porque es único como jugador y como persona"
articles.summary: "Wembanyama es un rival especial porque es único como jugador y como persona"
articles.body: Nikola Jokic (31 años y 2,11 m.) reconoció el talento de Victor Wembanyama (22 años y 2,24 m.) después del triunfo de Serbia ante Francia por 90-87, en el que el jugador serbio rozó el triple-doble con 20 puntos, 9 rebotes y 8 asistencias en el Belgrade Arena. "Wembanyama es un rival especial porque es único como jugador y como persona. No lo veo como un rival y no me lo tomo como algo personal. Victor la oportunidad de ser el jugador de baloncesto más único que jamás hayamos visto: de ser el mejor de la historia", reconoció Jokic, ganador de la NBA en 2023 y tres veces MVP (2021, 2022, 2024). Victor Wembayama terminó el partido contra Serbia con 10 puntos, 5 rebotes y 2 asistencias para 10 de valoración. Respecto al triunfo de Serbia ante Francia apuntó que "fue una buena prueba para nosotros contra un rival de calidad al que le faltaban varios jugadores de la Euroliga y de la NBA. Son peligrosos, pero logramos controlar el partido durante la mayor parte del tiempo antes de sufrir un bajón. Al final, fue un buen partido para nosotros".

articles.title: "Campazzo iba a 300 kilómetros por hora"
articles.standfirst: Ognjen Dobric recuerda el paso de Facundo Campazzo por el Estrella Roja antes de regresar al Real Madrid
articles.summary: Ognjen Dobric recuerda el paso de Facundo Campazzo por el Estrella Roja antes de regresar al Real Madrid
articles.body: Ognjen Dobric, capitán del Estrella Roja que esta temporada entrena el español Ibon Navarro y excompañero del Facundo Campazzo en el equipo de Belgrado la temporada 2022–2023, habló sobre el base del Real Madrid en el podcast '6.75range'. "Campazzo siempre estaba esprintando. Iba a 300 kilómetros por hora; nunca había visto algo así", compartió el escolta de 31 años sobre el base del Real Madrid. Dobric destacó que "Campazzo no se cansaba. Y Dusko Ivanovic (el entonces entrenador del Estrella Roja) ama a los jugadores así. Todos empezamos a alimentarnos de esa energía". "El mayor nombre del equipo llega y es el que más duro entrena. Te sientes estúpido si no trabajas. Y además sabe tanto de baloncesto… Sabe exactamente qué jugada marcar y cuándo. A quién atacar. Es un líder increíble. Nunca decía: "Dusko, lo hacemos a mi manera". Siempre respetaba", recuerda Dobric sobre el paso de Campazzo por el Estrella Roja. Facundo Campazzo llegó al Estrella Roja tras dejar la NBA, y en Serbia promedió 13 puntos y 6,5 asistencias en la Liga Adriática y 15 puntos y 5,9 asistencias en Euroliga. El 18 de julio de 2023 fichaba por el Real Madrid. Respecto a los métodos de trabajo de Ivanovic compartió que "Dusko es un hombre muy justo. Con él, te ganas los minutos en los entrenamientos. Si no entrenabas el día antes del partido, no jugabas. Si alguien estaba bien en el entrenamiento, jugaba veinte minutos. Todos lo sabían así que iban al máximo, recordó. Ognjen Dobric se atrevió a confeccionar un quinteto de los mejores jugadores extranjeros con los que coincidió en el Estrella Roja, y eligió de primeras a Facundo Campazzo, Jared Butler, Marco Belinelli, Tornike Shengelia y Bryant Dunston. "Vale, ahora necesito un 'cuatro'. Había nombres de todo tipo: Shengelia, Moneke, Johnny O'Bryant... ¿Te acuerdas de Johnny?. ¿Quién más estaba...? Nadie sabe dónde está Johnny O'Bryant. Cuando apareció, en la temporada del coronavirus—, el entrenador Dejo Radonjic lo había echado.Lo echó, pero cuando íbamos a la Copa en Novi Sad ahí estaba él, delante del autobús. Le pregunto: "¿Qué haces aquí?", y me dice: "Me llamaron para ir con vosotros". Lo habían echado, hermano; plena pandemia, nos faltaba un jugador. Lo llamaron, vino, cumplió con su trabajo, regresó de Novi Sad, aparcó frente al Pionir y nunca más lo volvimos a ver", recordó Ognjen Dobric entre risas.

articles.title: El niño de 2,36 que probó el Madrid al fin explota: llega el momento de Rioux y sus 2,44 de envergadura
articles.standfirst: Olivier Rioux ha pasado de promediar 0,6 puntos y 0,5 rebotes en 1,5 minutos con Florida a sumar 9 puntos, 11 rebotes, 2 asistencias y 1 tapón en 16 minutos con UC Irvine
articles.summary: Olivier Rioux ha pasado de promediar 0,6 puntos y 0,5 rebotes en 1,5 minutos con Florida a sumar 9 puntos, 11 rebotes, 2 asistencias y 1 tapón en 16 minutos con UC Irvine
articles.body: Olivier Rioux, el pívot de 2,36 metros de altura y 2,44 metros de envergadura que probó el Real Madrid, ha jugado sus primeros partidos con UC Irvine tras su traspaso desde Florida. El jugador más alto de la historia de la NCAA sumó en su último partido 9 puntos, 11 rebotes, 2 asistencias y 1 tapón en 16 minutos. Olivier Roux, que tiene 20 años, promedió 0,6 puntos y 0,5 rebotes en 1,5 minutos en los 11 partidos que disputó la pasada temporada con Florida tras pasar un año sin jugar como 'redshirt'. Olivier Rioux fue considerado el adolescente más alto del mundo y es 5 centímetros más alto que Gheorghe Mureșan y Manute Bol, los dos jugadores más altos en la historia de la NBA, y 7 centímetros más alto que Yao Ming, Tacko Fall y Shawn Bradley. Olivier Rioux, que cuando tenía 15 años ya medía 2,26 m., estuvo probando con la cantera del Real Madrid y disputó con el equipo merengue el Torneo U13 de Castelldefels. El Madrid captó al gigante canadiense, que oficialmente se convirtió en el adolescente más alto del mundo, en el Torneo de La Roda de 2018 que disputó con 13 años y jugó con el equipo francés Frenchy Phenoms. Finalmente Olivier Rioux no se incorporó a la cantera del Real Madrid, y decidió seguir con su formación en Brookwood Elite y en la prestigiosa academia de formación IMG Academy de Florida.

articles.title: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert Says Others Are Trying to 'Sow Divisiveness' in Transgender Debate
articles.summary: DALLAS (AP) — WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert denounced people she said are trying to "sow divisiveness" as the league grapples with a debate over transgender athletes.
articles.body:
DALLAS (AP) — WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert denounced people she said are trying to "sow divisiveness" as the league grapples with a debate over transgender athletes.

Engelbert made the comments Thursday before the Indiana Fever's 91-85 loss to the Dallas Wings at the home of the Dallas Mavericks.

Demonstrators showed up outside American Airlines Center, as they have at other venues since the Fever's Sophie Cunningham voiced support for barring transgender girls and women from girls' and women's sports in an extensive ESPN profile.

Source: Freedom, White Not Eligible for WNBA Draft (AP)

Sky Ban Enes Kanter Freedom from Home Games (AP)

The league issued a statement last week criticizing efforts to make an issue about the eligibility of transgender athletes in the WNBA. Engelbert's comments in a pregame gathering in Dallas were her first since the league called out what it said were bad faith efforts to use the debate to "demean or marginalize others."

"People are trying to use the league to sow divisiveness," Engelbert said Thursday while sitting alongside Wings CEO and managing partner Greg Bibb.

"We're being the center of political football for people who have never watched the WNBA, never have written about the WNBA or reported on the WNBA," Engelbert said, echoing NBA Commissioner Adam Silver's recent use of "political football" to describe the debate that has engulfed the WNBA.

The league's collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," but it does not include any more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth. Earlier this month, two former NBA players, Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White, declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women.

Engelbert sent a memo this month to team presidents and general managers saying the league would discuss the subject of transgender women in women's basketball.

"There's always going to be haters out there and we denounce it," Engelebert said Thursday. "But that's what happens when you have made it as a legitimate sports media and entertainment product."

articles.title: Angel Reese Makes WNBA History, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Beat Brink, Sparks
articles.summary: Angel Reese's perfect shooting night helped the Atlanta Dream cruise to an easy 124-88 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Angel Reese's perfect shooting night helped the Atlanta Dream cruise to an easy 124-88 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.

The Dream, who entered the night favored by 8.5 points at FanDuel Sportsbook , had no problem covering en route to earning their fourth win in the last five games.

Reese became the first player in WNBA history to have a game with at least 20 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and three steals without missing a shot from the field.

Reese joined Nikola Jokić as the only players in NBA and WNBA history have that stat line. Jokić did it during the 2018-19 season when he had 35 points on 11-of-11 shooting, 11 rebounds, 11 assists and four steals for the Denver Nuggets in a win over the Phoenix Suns.

A segment of Reese's night included going on a personal 10-0 run against the Sparks defense in the second quarter. The Dream led by as many as 42 points at one point. Their 124 points tied the second-highest output by any team this season.

Per the Associated Press , Reese is the third player in WNBA history with a 20-point double-double without a missed field goal. She also set the Dream record for most field-goals without a miss in a game.

Reese also recorded her league-leading 25th double-double of the season in the process. Dallas Wings forward Jessica Shepard is the only other player with 20 double-doubles.

The win moved Atlanta (23-13) one-half game behind the Indiana Fever for the No. 4 seed and homecourt advantage in the first round of the playoffs with eight games remaining in the regular season.

Next up for Reese and the Dream is a matchup with the Phoenix Mercury on Saturday at Mortgage Matchup Center.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Reacts to NBA 2K27 Player Rating in New Video After Trade to 76ers from Celtics
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown had some qualms with 2K after his player rating in NBA 2K27 was revealed.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown had some qualms with 2K after his player rating in NBA 2K27 was revealed.

Brown said he was "offended" that his mid-range rating was only a 90 since he is a "spammer" in that area of the court, and he also questioned how his overall rating dropped two points to 91 after being 93 last year.

It is a bit hard to justify Brown's overall rating going down when he just finished sixth in MVP voting. Even with all of the handwringing over his efficiency, he was the main piece for a Boston Celtics team that won 56 games last season.

Brown will be bringing his 91 overall rating to the Sixers after a surprise trade with Boston in the offseason. He is part of a new-look Philadelphia roster that also added LeBron James to play alongside Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

articles.title: James Harden's Pay Cut, Peyton Watson Recruitment Detailed in New NBA Rumors After Cavs Contract
articles.summary: Veteran guard James Harden was reportedly both flexible and influential during the Cleveland Cavaliers' pursuit of Peyton Watson.
articles.body:
Veteran guard James Harden was reportedly both flexible and influential during the Cleveland Cavaliers' pursuit of Peyton Watson.

In the wake of the Cavs acquiring Watson from the Denver Nuggets this week, ESPN NBA insider Brian Windhorst provided some insight into Harden's role in the process on Friday's episode of Brian Windhorst & The Hoop Collective (beginning at the 12-minute mark) .

"James Harden was willing to opt out of that contract and sit around all summer, and basically pick up the phone whenever the Cavs called and say, 'Yeah, I'll go down a little farther. I'll go down a little farther,'" Windhorst said. "So as the Cavs made various moves, Harden was not only willing to reduce his salary, but he was willing to recruit. He—from what I understand—he recruited Peyton Watson."

The Watson deal was agreed upon Wednesday, as the Cavs sent Max Strus to the Los Angeles Clippers and an unprotected 2031 first-round pick to the Nuggets as part of the three-team trade.

One day later, Harden's agents informed ESPN's Shams Charania that Harden had agreed to a three-year, $97 million contract to return to the Cavaliers.

It was considered a foregone conclusion throughout the offseason that Harden would re-sign with the Cavs, but he waited and allowed the organization to pursue other potential upgrades to the roster.

LeBron James' agent, Rich Paul, confirmed on his Game Over podcast (h/t Conor Smith of the Philadelphia Inquirer ) that the Cavs were among the finalists in the LeBron sweepstakes before he decided to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Had James chosen the Cavs, it would have marked his third stint with the organization he led to a championship in 2016.

Despite LeBron going elsewhere, Harden remained patient, and it paid off in the form of Cleveland adding Watson to the team's already impressive core of Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Mitchell.

Watson set career highs with 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 three-pointers made per game last season, and adding him to a Cavs team that reached the Eastern Conference Finals last season should make Cleveland an even more serious contender in 2026-27.

articles.title: Los Wolves cambian de dueño por 4.500 millones de dólares
articles.standfirst: Segunda venta de un equipo de la NBA en menos de un mes
articles.summary: Segunda venta de un equipo de la NBA en menos de un mes
articles.body: El empresario Marc Stad alcanzó un acuerdo para comprar los Minnesota Timberwolves y las Minnesota Lynx por 4.500 millones de dólares, según anunció este viernes la cadena ESPN. Stad, fundador del grupo inversor Dragoneer Investment Group, era hasta la fecha un socio minoritario en ambas franquicias, pero acordó la compra de la participación mayoritaria del empresario Marc Lore. Lore ejercía como copresidente de los dos equipos de la NBA y la WNBA junto con el exjugador de béisbol Álex Rodríguez, quien continuará en su cargo actual. Esta es la segunda venta de una franquicia de la NBA en el último mes, después de que el dueño de Los Ángeles Lakers, Mark Walter, alcanzara el 12 de agosto un acuerdo para vender la franquicia angelina a los empresarios Josh Kushner y Bob Iger por 12.000 millones de dólares. La venta de los Timberwolves y las Lynx es la cuarta operación más alta en la historia de la NBA. Además de la ya mencionada venta de los Lakers a Kushner e Iger, la franquicia angelina pasó a manos de Walter el año pasado tras comprarla por cerca de 10.000 millones de dólares a la familia Buss, propietaria de los angelinos desde 1979. Los eternos rivales del equipo de oro y púrpura, los Boston Celtics, también cambiaron de propietario hace un año a cambio de 6.100 millones de dólares.

Lore ejercía como copresidente de los dos equipos de la NBA y la WNBA junto con el exjugador de béisbol Álex Rodríguez, quien continuará en su cargo actual. Esta es la segunda venta de una franquicia de la NBA en el último mes, después de que el dueño de Los Ángeles Lakers, Mark Walter, alcanzara el 12 de agosto un acuerdo para vender la franquicia angelina a los empresarios Josh Kushner y Bob Iger por 12.000 millones de dólares. La venta de los Timberwolves y las Lynx es la cuarta operación más alta en la historia de la NBA. Además de la ya mencionada venta de los Lakers a Kushner e Iger, la franquicia angelina pasó a manos de Walter el año pasado tras comprarla por cerca de 10.000 millones de dólares a la familia Buss, propietaria de los angelinos desde 1979. Los eternos rivales del equipo de oro y púrpura, los Boston Celtics, también cambiaron de propietario hace un año a cambio de 6.100 millones de dólares.

articles.title: Otro recital de España para meterse en la gran final
articles.standfirst: La selección femenina sub 16 luchará por el oro este sábado (19.30) ante Eslovenia
articles.summary: La selección femenina sub 16 luchará por el oro este sábado (19.30) ante Eslovenia
articles.body: La selección española femenina sub 16 ya está en la final del Eurobasket. Era lo más probable dado el camino que había seguido hasta la semifinal. Tras cinco partidos llegaba al duelo ante Letonia con una media de anotación de 110,8 puntos y cinco triunfos por una ventaja media de 79,2. Un abuso en toda regla de un equipo que borda el baloncesto. Aunque Letonia fue el rival que más complicaciones dio al combinado que entrena Madelen Urieta, las bálticas también cayeron con cierto estrépito en una semifinal dominada por España (91-53). Un resultado que vuelve a sorprender y deja clara la calidad del equipo de España femenino sub 16. Letonia tenía claro el plan. No dejar a España correr y parar su ritmo con faltas. De hecho en el primer cuarto más igualado que ha jugado el combinado español (15-14), las de Urrieta fueron 20 veces a la línea de personal, fallando 11 de esos tiros. Además España tuvo problemas desde el triple, 0/9 iniciado el segundo cuarto. Pero la igualdad se acabó dos minutos después de comenzar el segundo acto. A 8:42 para el final Letonia se puso por delante, 15-16... y el partido se acabó. De ahí al final del cuarto España engrasó su maquinaria, mejoró la defensa y corrió, para arrollar a su rival. Un primer parcial de 12-0 que luego fue de 23-2 (38-18) abría de par en par la puerta de la final para España. Al descanso se llegó con 46-22 que dejaba el partido casi liquidado. España no bajó su ritmo en la reanudación elevando su ventaja sobre un equipo letón que se acabó entregando a la superioridad española. Amelia Alonso acabó con un doble-doble (16 puntos y 10 rebotes), Paula Reynal hizo 15+8, Aisha Mbengue aportó 12 pntos y Anastasia Lishchuk logró un 9+8. España buscará el oro, que sería el segundo consecutivo y el duodécimo en total, este sábado a partir de las 19.30 ante Eslovenia que se cargó a Francia en la otra semifinal, 58-67. En ese partido la pintura tendrá una batalla de apeliidos ilustres con Anastasia, hija de Sergei Lishchuk, ante Ema, hija de Erazem Lorbek.

articles.title: España saca buena nota en su examen contra Nigeria
articles.standfirst: Gana con claridad a las campeonas de África en un segundo tiempo arrollador
articles.summary: Gana con claridad a las campeonas de África en un segundo tiempo arrollador
articles.body: Aunque a España le faltan las cinco jugadoras de la WNBA, la preparación va dando pasos muy sólidos hacia lo que quiere Miguel Méndez: un equipo sin fisuras muy reconocible que crezca desde la defensa. Ante Nigeria mostró dos caras, una más frágil ante el planteamiento físico de las africanas, que duró algo menos de 20 minutos y otra, con una enorme mejoría defeniva y con vocación de correr. La segunda versión le valió el trunfo ante Nigeria (83-58) en el torneo internacional de Tenerife. Las campeonas africanas (lo son en las últimas cinco ediciones), asustaron al principio. Llegaron a tener cierta ventaja, 26-34 a falta de 3:17 para el final del segundo cuarto, y se fueron con 36-40 al decanso. Ese paso por vestuarios le sentó mucho mejor a España. Seguramente Méndez incidió en la defensa para empezar a construir el ataque y sus jugadoras lo interpretaron a la perfección. El partido cambió por completo, Nigeria anotó tan sólo nueve puntos en el tercer acto mientras que España, dominando el rebote, empezó a correr y a encontrar mayor efectividad en el tiro. Andrea Vilaró anotó cuatro triples, Iyana Martín tres y Mariona Ortiz, dos. La ventaja de España fue creciendo hasta los 25 puntos finales que fue la mayor ventaja de la selección. El parcial tras el descanso fue de 47-18 para las de Méndez en una muestra de hacia dónde fueron capaces de llevar el choque. El colapso nigeriano fue total ante un equipo que se había convertido en un vendaval. España acabó liderada en puntos por Iyana Martín (12), seguida por Helena Pueyo (11) y Mariona Ortiz (10). Destacaron también los siete rebotes de Irati Etxarri, que fue una de las jugadores que impregnaron de defensa el juego de la selección. La mejor anotadora del partido fue la nigeriana Macaulay (18). Es sólo una prueba, la segunda de España tras ganar a Alemania (60-65), pero puede dar una idea del trabajo que se ha hecho en el equipo en este tiempo de preparación. La siguiente será este domingo Bélgica (21.00).

articles.title: Knicks' Jose Alvarado Gives Inside Scoop on Josh Hart at KAT, Jordyn Woods' Wedding
articles.summary: Josh Hart's ability as the New York Knicks' do-it-all Swiss Army Knife apparently extends beyond the basketball court and onto the dance floor.
articles.body:
Josh Hart's ability as the New York Knicks' do-it-all Swiss Army Knife apparently extends beyond the basketball court and onto the dance floor.

Speaking to TMZ Sports about the wedding between Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods, Knicks guard Jose Alvarado declared Hart was the best dancer of anyone at the event.

Alvarado also spoke about the ceremony itself, praising the environment.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

"Definitely different to be in that room, but it was dope," Alvarado said. "You know, everybody, no matter what level you are, everybody's human, so it was just cool to be around that. ... It was cool to see all those people show up and, you know, come out for our brother."

Towns and Woods got married in Malibu last weekend. The star-studded guest list included Michael B. Jordan, Knicks superfans Timothée Chalamet and Ben Stiller.

The wedding capped off a huge summer for Towns, who helped lead the Knicks to their first NBA championship in 53 years. They went 16-3 through the playoffs, including 13 consecutive wins at one point.

articles.title: Mark Mitchell Commits to Kentucky in Transfer Portal, Former 5-Star Also Played for Duke, Missouri
articles.summary: Forward Mark Mitchell will indeed be staying in college after a temporary injunction granted him a fifth season of college eligibility.
articles.body:
Forward Mark Mitchell will indeed be staying in college after a temporary injunction granted him a fifth season of college eligibility.

According to On3's Joe Tipton , Mitchell will be joining the Kentucky Wildcats in the transfer portal.

Mitchell went through the NBA draft process and signed an Exhibit-10 contract with the Denver Nuggets, having exhausted his eligibility last season. But new NCAA rules this offseason allow players up to five years of eligibility within a five-year period, though Mitchell's class wasn't included in that ruling.

In response, Mitchell joined a lawsuit contesting his lack of eligibility. He and the other players in the case were granted a temporary injunction by Jefferson County Circuit Court Judge Brian Edwards.

Similar rulings elsewhere have cast a lot of uncertainty regarding eligibility and the transfer portal across the college football and basketball landscape:

Mitchell's addition would be a pretty huge one for Kentucky. The former Duke and Missouri forward averaged 18.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists for the Tigers last season, shooting 54.7 percent from the field and 38.8 percent from three.

Mark Pope hit the transfer portal hard, landing the No. 1 class in that regard. That helped cover for a more modest year in recruiting and followed the recent trend of more veteran-laden squads winning the national championship. Mitchell would further improve Kentucky's chances.

Much depends on the NCAA's response to the various court rulings impacting the sport, but for now, Kentucky has landed a major contributor for next season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Sabrina Ionescu, Sophie Cunningham's Final Stats, Highlights as Liberty Beat Fever
articles.summary: Sabrina Ionescu and the New York Liberty won a high-scoring affair against Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and the Indiana Fever on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Sabrina Ionescu and the New York Liberty won a high-scoring affair against Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and the Indiana Fever on Saturday night.

The Liberty, who were a 1.5-point favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook, held on for a 108-102 victory.

Ionescu was one of four Liberty starters in double figures. She scored 12 points, while Breanna Stewart had 22 and Leonie Fiebich produced 20.

Ionescu added four assists and three rebounds to her 12-point outing.

Clark was one of three Fever players to score over 20 points in the defeat.

The Fever star had 11 rebounds and assists to go along with her 21 points and pair of three-pointers.

Cunningham was the only bench player on either side to reach double digits with 10 points.

The Fever played from behind for a majority of the second half and could not complete a comeback on the road.

New York moved to 23-15 with the victory, while Indiana dropped to 24-14. The two teams are now just a game apart in the multi-team race for the No. 2 seed.

articles.title: Angel Reese Has Career Night, Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Clinch Playoffs vs. Mercury
articles.summary: Angel Reese enjoyed a career night as the Atlanta Dream sealed their place in the WNBA playoffs.
articles.body:
Angel Reese enjoyed a career night as the Atlanta Dream sealed their place in the WNBA playoffs.

The third-year forward had 31 points in a 99-89 win over the Phoenix Mercury on Saturday. She posted her 26th double-double of the season thanks to grabbing 14 rebounds.

"I think she keeps getting better and keeps being able to expand her game," Dream coach Karl Smesko said, per ESPN.com . "I think she really found her opportunities to be physical. They weren't really sending doubles, so she had her opportunities to catch the ball in the short and do some post moves to score. She was able to get behind on some ball screens for some layups where our guards were able to find her, got a couple of putbacks.

"She was scoring in a multitude of ways, had a really great fourth quarter for us, and it's good to see her have one of her best games of her career, offensively."

Reese did a lot of damage around the basket, taking full advantage of Phoenix's lack of depth in the frontcourt. Only three of her points came from the charity stripe.

The three-time All-Star has made a conscious effort to widen her range, though it remains a work in progress.

Reese's 50 three-point attempts are more than double her previous high (22), but she's shooting just 18 percent from deep. Her overall efficiency hasn't improved, either, as she's knocking down 47.3 percent of her two-pointers, nearly equal to her 2025 output (47.8 percent).

The postseason figures to be a major test for Reese and the Dream as a whole. She didn't taste playoff basketball during her two years with the Chicago Sky, while Atlanta is coming off a disappointing first-round exit a season ago.

Games often slow down in the playoffs, and spacing the floor becomes more imperative. Players such as Reese, who aren't reliable three-point threats, can be exploited by opposing coaches.

Assuming she doesn't suddenly blossom into a stretch 4 over the next month, Reese may nonetheless remain effective through her rebounding and relentless motor in the paint.

The Dream, meanwhile, are clearly looking to her to provide something they were lacking when they got bounced by the Indiana Fever.

articles.title: Dr. J Reacts to LeBron, Jaylen Brown Joining 76ers and Sounds Off on NBA Title Chances
articles.summary: While Philadelphia 76ers legend Julius Erving believes the team improved this offseason, he's not immediately crowning them NBA champions.
articles.body:
While Philadelphia 76ers legend Julius Erving believes the team improved this offseason, he's not immediately crowning them NBA champions.

Erving told TMZ Sports he gave the Sixers a "thumbs up" for the Jaylen Brown trade, adding they will be "one of the most talented teams." The Hall of Famer does, however, have some questions about a lineup that includes 41-year-old LeBron James and 21-year-old VJ Edgecombe.

"There's a big age discrepancy between the youngest, you know, which is VJ, and LeBron," he said. "So how that works, it remains to be seen."

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Erving compared the roster to experimenting with a new dish in the kitchen you've never tried.

"You're trying to create something special. You're trying to create something," he said. "You go in the kitchen and you mix the ingredients, and then once you put fire under there, you see whether it's going to be good, great, or OK."

Erving's assessment probably represents the general consensus on Philadelphia.

On paper, a starting five of James, Brown, Edgecombe, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey is the best in the NBA. Getting all of the pieces to fit together could be tricky, though, when four of the five are accustomed to working on the ball.

Philly is also hedging a lot of its hopes on Embiid staying healthy, which is a familiar concern. The team's ceiling changes if he's not on the floor because there's a steep drop between he and backup center Adem Bona.

The Sixers have the talent to challenge the New York Knicks for the Eastern Conference crown. Still, NBA superteams haven't fared well in recent years, so it won't be a complete shock if the experiment proves to be a bust.

articles.title: Updated 2026 WNBA Playoffs Bracket Picture and Standings After Sonia Citron, Mystics Clinch Berth
articles.summary: The Washington Mystics earned their first WNBA playoff berth since 2023 with Sunday's win over the Portland Fire paired with a loss from the Chicago Sky.
articles.body:
The Washington Mystics earned their first WNBA playoff berth since 2023 with Sunday's win over the Portland Fire paired with a loss from the Chicago Sky.

Washington is on pace to secure the No. 7 seed, sitting at 22-15.

No Cunningham-Carrington Issues in Rematch (AP)

2. Golden State Valkyries (25-11); clinched

11. Los Angeles Sparks (13-24); eliminated

The Mystics lost 28 games and finished seven back of the eighth-place Golden State Valkyries in 2025. The general vibes around the organization were not those of a team that was well outside of the postseason hunt, though.

That's because Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen both made the All-Star team as rookies, and the 2026 WNBA draft promised to bring more reinforcements for a young core.

Citron is averaging more points (16.9) and assists (4.1) than she did last year, and Iriafen has seen a bump to her scoring (15.1) and rebounds (9.3). Both are taking steps forward in their development.

Shakira Austin, meanwhile, has expanded her offensive repertoire. Seventeed made three-pointers may not seem like a lot, but they are for a player who knocked down three total threes through her first four seasons.

Depth behind the starting rotation has come from 2026 first-rounders Lauren Betts and Cotie McMahon. Georgia Amoore, who missed her entire rookie campaign through injury, is second on the team in assists (3.5).

Ironically, the 25-year-old Amoore is one of the oldest players.

Washington is bucking almost every historic precedent. Teams with rosters this young have by and large been very, very bad.

Even when accounting for the fact the WNBA has diluted the talent pool a bit through expansion, putting together a winning record when only three players on the roster have more than one year of service time is incredible.

For right now, the Mystics are playing with house money because they're ahead of schedule in their rebuild. Winning a series would be nice, but simply having Citron, Iriafen, Betts and McMahon taste playoff basketball is important in its own right.

The postseason could also be instructive to the coaching staff and front office toward how to continue building around Citron and Iriafen.
